title: Coordinate clipping: Real Stability
abstract: \leanpath{coordinate-clipping} uses interval clamp, which is $1$-Lipschitz; hence $|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$ implies the clamped values move by at most $\varepsilon$. Lean \texttt{LEAN\_FULL}.
stability: Nonexpansiveness of clamp: output perturbation $\le$ input perturbation in absolute value.
definitions: Require $\mathrm{lo}\le\mathrm{hi}$. Stability form is the Lipschitz claim with $|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$.
intuition: Clipping cannot expand distances: points move weakly toward the interval.
proof: The map $x\mapsto\max(\mathrm{lo},\min(x,\mathrm{hi}))$ is $1$-Lipschitz on $\mathbb{R}$ when $\mathrm{lo}\le\mathrm{hi}$ (standard case analysis on the three regions $(-\infty,\mathrm{lo}]$, $[\mathrm{lo},\mathrm{hi}]$, $[\mathrm{hi},\infty)$). Therefore $|\mathrm{clamp}(x')-\mathrm{clamp}(x)|\le|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:inv}). Sharpness: take an interior segment of length $\varepsilon$ inside $[\mathrm{lo},\mathrm{hi}]$.
consequences: Interval/box/clipping operators reduce to clamp. Related: projection-interval, coordinate-clipping.
